name: samurai
intent: Side-view (+X) two-handed katana overhead cut: feet stay in a slight open static stance; both arms/forearms rotate until hands coincide on an imagined katana grip, raise the blade overhead, then slash down through a vertical cut.

beats.pose_description: Ready: feet slightly open and planted (static for whole clip); both hands already meeting on an imagined katana grip held in front of the chest/waist, elbows bent so forearms converge.
Wind-up start: legs unchanged; both arms lift together as one unit, keeping hands locked on the shared grip, katana rising toward the head.
Raise mid: arms continue upward in sync; elbows adjust so near and far forearms stay coincident on the grip; blade climbs above the jingasa line.
Apex: katana fully overhead (or slightly behind the head); both upper arms raised and stacked, forearms meeting on the grip above; slight neck lean into the cut prep; feet still static open stance.
Slash start: both arms begin the downward cut as one rigid two-hand grip; blade arcs from overhead toward forward/+X; legs still planted.
Slash mid: arms sweep through horizontal/chest height still locked together; strongest silhouette of the vertical tajo.
Impact/follow-through: two-hand grip finishes low-forward; elbows extend the cut past the waist toward +X; weight stays on the static open stance.
Settle: cut ends with blade low-front, hands still together on the grip; tiny settle of elbows/neck, feet unchanged — readable end pose of the overhead slash.

plan.silhouette_story: Eight-frame side attack facing +X: planted open stance never steps. Arms lock together as if gripping a two-handed katana, raise the blade overhead, then deliver a single downward slash through the front. Reads as a deliberate shomen/jodan cut, not a walk, run, or punch.

differs_from.walk: Walk cycles opposite-limb stride with marching arm pendulum; attack keeps feet static and drives both arms together through an overhead raise and downward cut.
differs_from.run: Run is airborne locomotor with opposite arm pump and high knee flight; attack is a rooted two-hand sword cut with coinciding hands and no stride.

plan.weapon_or_style_notes: Imagined two-handed katana (no separate weapon layer): near and far shoulders/elbows must be authored so hands visually coincide on one grip. Motion is raise-to-overhead then vertical/forward downward tajo — not a one-hand slash, jab, or empty-hand punch.
